- Integrated manufacturing capabilities — two Pune facilities equipped with melting furnaces and ladle furnace, casting machines for GDC, LPDC and HPDC, high-precision machining equipment, heat treatment furnaces and induction hardening equipment, and testing equipment including spectro analysis instruments, hardness testing machines, density index units, vacuum analysers, leak-testing systems, universal testing machines, CMM and 3D scanning and inspection systems

- In-house design and engineering functions with a 17-employee team using tools such as Adstefan casting simulation software and Solidcam Bundle standard software, plus reverse engineering supported by X-ray machines for internal structure assessment
- Quality management systems and certifications — ISO 14001:2015, ISO 45001:2018, ISO 9001:2015 and IATF 16949:2016 for both manufacturing facilities, with periodic audits by customers and certification authorities
- Diversified and growing customer base — from 39 customers in Fiscal 2024 to 58 customers in Fiscal 2026, with repeated business generated from 25 customers over the periods
- Manufacturing facilities located in close proximity to each other, which has benefitted the Company by optimizing production and delivery solutions
- Awards received from customers for quality excellence, product development and supplier performance, including Best Project Award-I Quality Improvement, Innovative Approach for Development, Quality Excellence Award, Best Casting Competition, Best Supplier Award and Gold Award
- Experienced leadership — Chairman with around 32 years in aluminium die casting, tooling and engineering manufacturing; Managing Director with over 16 years in casting and engineering; Whole Time Director with over 25 years in alloy manufacturing, casting and engineering
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Reliance on a limited number of key customers and Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) — More than 70% of revenue from operations came from the top five customers during the last 3 fiscal years; Customer 1 alone was 31.75% of total sales in FY 2026 (34.63% in FY 2025, 41.94% in FY 2024) and the top ten customers were 88.64% / 90.63% / 96.00%. Any cancellation, loss or reduction of orders could materially affect revenue and business operations.
- No firm volume commitments — sales run on purchase orders — The Company generally does not enter into long-term purchase agreements with these customers, or where entered they set out only general terms and do not stipulate firm volume or sales commitments. Purchase orders / delivery schedules may be cancelled unilaterally with or without cause, or there may be delays in lifting goods, adversely impacting revenue and results of operations.
- OEM and tier-1 qualification dependence — Before being appointed as a supplier to OEMs or their vendors in the automotive and electric vehicle segments, the Company must pass a qualification and assessment process including facility evaluations, process audits and testing of sample components; components also undergo customer-specific inspection and validation before purchase orders are issued, and facilities are subject to periodic audits by customers and certification authorities.
- Execution and funding risk on the proposed Unit III — Unit III at Gat No. 382, 383, 386, 387, 312 Village, Tal.-Khed, Dist.-Pune is still to be established and depends on the net proceeds of the Issue, with Rs. 10633.59 lakhs earmarked; the Issue Price, Gross Proceeds and Net Proceeds all remain undetermined ([●]) in the Red Herring Prospectus.
- Magnesium diversification is still pre-approval — Unit IV is being set up only to carry out sample development and submission activities for magnesium precision components until customer and OEM approvals are obtained — commercial production is contingent on approvals not yet received.
- Geographic concentration of revenue in Maharashtra and volatile exports — Maharashtra accounted for 60.64% of revenue as at March 31, 2026 (65.50% in FY 2025, 68.44% in FY 2024); exports were only Rs. 248.2 lakhs / 0.84% in FY 2026 versus Rs. 716.69 lakhs / 3.23% in FY 2025, indicating a volatile international revenue stream.
- Capacity utilization gap after a step-up in installed capacity — Installed melting capacity rose to 13800 MT in 2025-26 from 9300 MT and 7800 MT in the prior two years, with utilization at 80% (melting) and 84% (casting & finishing); utilization had previously dipped to 72% and 70% in 2024-25, and final orders received may fluctuate based on demand at that time.
- Aerospace entry is only at vendor-approval stage — The Company states it has recently entered the aerospace segment and obtained vendor approval from a customer for the supply of its products; no aerospace revenue appears in the sector revenue tables for 23-24, 24-25 or 25-26.

business.body: Poojaa Precision Engg. Limited manufactures aluminium die casting and machining components using gravity die casting (GDC), low-pressure die casting (LPDC) and high-pressure die casting (HPDC), supported by in-house melting, casting, cleaning, machining, assembly and related engineering services. It supplies the automotive sector (brackets, intake manifolds, cylinder head covers, camshaft carriers, clutch housings, oil filter holders, elbow assemblies), the electric vehicle mobility sector (transmission housings, brackets, housing bearing sleeve assembly) and non-automotive sectors spanning agriculture, defence, energy, healthcare and engineering goods. Customers include original equipment manufacturers and tier-1 automotive suppliers in the domestic market, with automobile component exports to Germany, United States, Italy and Switzerland.

outlook.body: The Company operates two manufacturing facilities in Chakan, Pune — Unit 1 at Gat No. 253/1A (operational since 2007, also the Registered Office) and Unit 2 at Gat No. 251/1, Plot Nos. 9, 10, 11, 13 (operational since 2021, established to address increasing demand) — with a combined melting capacity of 13800 MT (annual) and casting and finishing capacity of approx. 6000MT (annual) as on March 31, 2026. Installed melting capacity has been scaled from 7800 MT in 2023-24 to 9300 MT in 2024-25 to 13800 MT in 2025-26, and casting & finishing from 3900 MT to 4800 MT to 6000 MT over the same periods, with utilization of 80% (melting) and 84% (casting & finishing) in 2025-26. The Company is in the process of establishing an additional manufacturing unit in Pune ("Unit III") at Gat No. 382, 383, 386, 387, 312 Village, Tal. - Khed, Dist. - Pune, which will be used for the production of components similar to those manufactured at the existing facilities by utilizing the net proceeds from the IPO (Rs. 10633.59 lakhs earmarked in the Objects of the Issue). Separately, the Company is undertaking a diversification into the manufacturing of precision components using magnesium and is setting up Unit IV at Gat No. 201/1, Village - Mahalunge, Tal. - Khed, Dist. - Pune, to carry out sample development and submission activities for magnesium components until customer and OEM approvals are obtained. Two solar projects are proposed on farmland at Village Bhaganurwadi, Tal- Mukhed, Dist. Nanded, with a further parcel there earmarked for future use. The Company has also recently entered the aerospace segment and obtained vendor approval from a customer for the supply of its products.

outlook.body:
- Sector mix shift — automobile sector share of revenue moved from 79.87% in 23-24 to 72.05% in 24-25 and 72.58% in 25-26, while the EV sector rose from 6.13% to 8.75% to 9.81% and the non-automobile sector from 14.00% to 19.21% to 17.61%
- Capacity utilization as a throughput lever — melting utilization 77% (2023-24), 72% (2024-25), 80% (2025-26); casting & finishing utilization 77%, 70% and 84% over the same periods, against installed capacity stepped up from 7800/3900 MT to 13800/6000 MT
- Purchase-order based operating model — customers provide estimated order quantities on a periodic basis and final orders may fluctuate based on demand, which the Company uses to aim to keep manufacturing lines operating at optimum levels
- Cost optimization, productivity improvement and capacity utilization are stated responsibilities of the Managing Director in driving profitability
- Margin improvement through effective product costing, yield optimization and price negotiations, plus commercial negotiations with OEMs, Tier-1 customers and export clients and management of raw material procurement and vendor contracts, are stated responsibilities of the Whole Time Director
- Customer concentration and repeat business — customer base up from 39 (Fiscal 2024) to 58 (Fiscal 2026) with repeat business from 25 customers, while the top ten customers contributed 96.00% of sales in FY 2024, 90.63% in FY 2025 and 88.64% in FY 2026
- Geographic mix — Maharashtra's share of revenue fell from 68.44% (March 31, 2024) to 65.50% (March 31, 2025) to 60.64% (March 31, 2026), with Haryana rising from 0.80% to 6.15% and exports moving 0.54% to 3.23% to 0.84%
- Value-added processes — machining, assembly and related engineering services alongside casting, with dies sales and consumables as separate revenue lines
- Financials are prepared under Indian GAAP, the Companies Act and SEBI (ICDR) Regulations and restated per the peer reviewed auditor's report dated July 07, 2026; EBITDA is defined as Profit before tax + Depreciation + Total Interest Expenses - Other Income

Backward linkage is not integrated: aluminium (72.43% / 76.29% / 74.20% of raw material consumed in FY26/FY25/FY24) and other alloys are procured from third-party suppliers on purchase orders with no firm-commitment or exclusive arrangements and a limited qualified-supplier base. Forward: direct B2B supply to OEMs and tier-1 automotive suppliers on purchase orders and delivery schedules without long-term firm-volume contracts; exports to Germany, United States, Italy and Switzerland. Power sourced from the state electricity board plus solar panels at facilities, with a proposed Rs. 1481.43 lakhs captive solar project (power and fuel = 7.79% / 7.27% / 7.30% of total expenses in FY26/FY25/FY24); STP and ETP plants recycle and reuse water.

overview.business_model: Melts, die-casts (gravity die casting, low-pressure die casting and high-pressure die casting) and machines aluminium components at two Chakan, Pune manufacturing facilities - combined melting capacity 13800 MT (annual) and casting and finishing capacity of approx. 6000MT (annual) as on March 31, 2026 - offering integrated solutions covering design, engineering, melting, casting, cleaning and value-added processes including machining, assembly and related engineering services across over 600 SKUs, including certain safety-critical components. Sales are to original equipment manufacturers and tier-1 automotive suppliers in the domestic market plus exports to Germany, United States, Italy and Switzerland, and include die sales and consumables. FY 25-26 revenue from operations of Rs. 29,385.54 lakhs split: Automobile Sector Rs. 21,329.07 lakhs (72.58%), EV Sector Rs. 2,882.72 lakhs (9.81%) and Non-automobile Sector Rs. 5,173.75 lakhs (17.61%). Customer base increased from 39 customers in Fiscal 2024 to 58 customers in Fiscal 2026 (approximately 56 in Fiscal 2025), with repeated business from 25 customers.

At incorporation, subscribers Jayshree Anil Kulkarni and Shivajirao Apparao Kulkarni agreed to subscribe to 10 equity shares each but applied and paid for one equity share each, and the subscriber sheets of the MOA and AOA were revised without intimating the ROC. Form CHG-1 for creation of charge under Section 77 of the Companies Act, 2013 (corresponding to Section 125 of the Companies Act, 1956) was inadvertently not filed on certain loans including a vehicle loan from Mercedes-Benz Financial Services India Pvt. Ltd., though no such outstanding loans remain as on the date of the RHP. Clerical errors and omissions include incomplete or unsigned attachments, typographical errors in resolutions, non-selection of director category in certain DIR-12 forms, discrepancies in Forms 23AC, 23AC XBRL and AOC-4 XBRL due to mismatch or omission of values, incorrect reporting of number of shares in Form 23B for FY 2005-06, incomplete transfer details in Form 20B for FY 2009-10 and 2011-12, mismatch in the category of directors in certain MGT-7 filings, non-disclosure of Company Secretary remuneration in MGT-7 for FY 2021-22 and 2022-23, incorrect reporting of the total number of shareholders in MGT-7 for FY 2015-16, and signed attachments not bearing the Company's stamp. The auditor included a remark that the accounting software used for maintaining books of account does not have an audit trail (edit log) facility for fiscal year 2024-25. No show cause notice received till date; any regulatory penalty will be paid from internal accruals and no IPO proceeds will be utilized.

compliance_legal.detail: The regulatory and policy environment is evolving and subject to change, which could adversely affect business, prospects and results of operations, and future amendments may affect tax benefits such as capital gains tax or tax on capital market transactions. The Government of India announced the union budget for Financial Year 2026 pursuant to which the Finance Act, 2025 amended the Income-tax Act, 1961 including capital gains tax rates with effect from the date of announcement of the Budget; the Company has not fully determined the effects. The Government introduced the Code on Wages, 2019, the Code on Social Security, 2020, the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 and the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 which regulates cross-border data transfer, establishes a Data Protection Board of India and provides for penalties on data fiduciaries. Parliament passed the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, repealing the Indian Penal Code, 1860, the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 respectively with effect from July 1, 2024. Investors can be subject to Indian taxes arising out of capital gains on the sale of the Equity Shares or dividend paid thereon.
compliance_legal.title: Changing laws, rules and regulations and legal uncertainties, including corporate and tax laws

compliance_legal.detail: Under foreign exchange regulations, transfers of shares between non-residents and residents are freely permitted subject to sectoral norms, pricing guidelines and RBI reporting requirements; otherwise prior regulatory approval is required. Pursuant to Press Note No. 3 (2020 Series) dated April 17, 2020 issued by DPIIT, incorporated as the proviso to Rule 6(a) of the FEMA Rules, investments where the beneficial owner of the equity shares is situated in or is a citizen of a country sharing a land border with India can only be made through the Government approval route as prescribed in the Consolidated FDI Policy dated October 15, 2020 and the FEMA Rules; subsequent changes in beneficial ownership also require Government approval, and these restrictions also apply to subscribers of offshore derivative instruments.
compliance_legal.title: Foreign investment restrictions under Indian law

compliance_legal.detail: The Competition Act, 2002 was enacted to prevent practices having an appreciable adverse effect on competition (AAEC) in India; any arrangement, understanding or action causing or likely to cause an AAEC is deemed void and attracts substantial penalties, and agreements among competitors on prices, production limits or market sharing are presumed to have an AAEC. The Act prohibits abuse of dominant position, and directors, managers, secretaries or other officers may be held guilty where contravention took place with their consent, connivance or neglect. The CCI has extra-territorial powers to investigate agreements, abusive conduct or combinations occurring outside India having an AAEC in India. The Competition (Amendment) Act, 2023 introduced deal value thresholds for combinations, expedited merger review timelines, codification of the lowest standard of 'control' and enhanced penalties for false or withheld material information.
compliance_legal.title: Adverse application or interpretation of competition laws

financial_valuation.detail: The business is capital intensive as the Company adds and upgrades manufacturing facilities, increases its product portfolio and invests in researching and developing new technologies and products. Actual future capital requirements may differ from estimates due to unforeseen delays or cost overruns, unanticipated expenses, regulatory changes, economic conditions, engineering design changes, weather related delays, technological changes and new opportunities. Additional financing may involve debt (increasing interest and repayment obligations and additional covenants) or equity (diluting existing shareholders). Significant working capital is required to finance raw material purchase and design and manufacture of products before customer payments; reduced advance payments or longer payment schedules would increase receivables and current borrowings.

financial_valuation.detail: Purchase orders are generally finalised prior to commencement of production, exposing the Company to increases in raw material and other input costs, particularly aluminium and other metals, between receipt of the purchase order and the date of manufacture and supply. Some customers allow adjustments through exchange of debit and credit notes under an agreed price revision mechanism, but full or timely pass-through is not assured; where pricing is determined or substantially influenced by customers, the ability to independently negotiate revised prices may be limited. Time lags between procurement and implementation of revised pricing may adversely impact margins, cash flows and working capital, and competitiveness may require absorbing discounts, price reductions or other commercial concessions.

financial_valuation.title: Ability to pay dividends dependent on future earnings and restrictive covenants

financial_valuation.detail: India's sovereign debt rating could be downgraded due to several factors including changes in tax or fiscal policy or a decline in India's foreign exchange reserves, all outside the Company's control. Borrowing costs and access to debt capital markets depend significantly on the sovereign credit ratings of India, and adverse revisions could affect the ability to raise additional external financing, the interest rates and other commercial terms available, and the trading price of the Equity Shares.
financial_valuation.title: Possible downgrade in India's sovereign debt ratings

financial_valuation.detail: Inflation rates in India have been volatile in recent years and India has experienced high inflation in the recent past. High fluctuations in inflation rates may make it more difficult to accurately estimate or control costs, and increased expenses may not be adequately passed on to customers, adversely affecting business, prospects, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows. It is unclear whether Government of India economic measures to combat high inflation will remain in effect.
financial_valuation.title: Rising inflation in India

financial_valuation.detail: The Indian economy and financial markets are significantly influenced by worldwide economic, financial and market conditions, and any financial turmoil, especially in the United States of America or Europe, may negatively impact the Indian economy. A loss in investor confidence in financial systems, particularly in other emerging markets, may cause increased volatility in Indian financial markets, which have experienced the contagion effect of global financial turmoil evident from the sharp decline in SENSEX, BSE's benchmark index, in the past.
financial_valuation.title: Instability in financial markets

internal_operational.detail: The Company derives more than 70% of revenue from operations from its top five customers in each of the last three fiscals. It generally does not enter into long-term purchase agreements; where entered, they set out general terms only and do not stipulate firm volume or sales commitments. It relies on purchase orders and delivery schedules that may be cancelled unilaterally with or without cause. Loss of, or reduced offtake from, these customers could materially affect revenue, results of operations and cash flow.
internal_operational.title: Reliance on a limited number of key customers and OEMs

internal_operational.detail: Cost of material consumed - primarily Aluminium, other alloys, dies and consumables - forms a significant portion of total expenses, and Aluminium is subject to commodity price fluctuation. Raw materials are procured from third parties on purchase orders without firm commitments or long-term fixed-price contracts, limiting the ability to resist supplier price increases. A time gap between procurement and resetting component prices for customers may adversely affect cash flows.
internal_operational.evidence: Risk factor 2 (Amt. in Rs. Lakhs), March 31, 2026 / March 31, 2025 / March 31, 2024: Raw Materials Consumed 13727.73 | 10078.26 | 7622.53; Aluminium 9943.04 | 7689.28 | 5655.99; Aluminium as % of raw material consumed 72.43% | 76.29% | 74.20%.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on availability and cost of raw materials, principally Aluminium

internal_operational.detail: Raw materials are procured via general purchase arrangements supplemented by purchase orders, typically valid until terminated by either party on prior notice. Strict customer quality requirements limit the supplier base, increasing the risk of being unable to make alternative arrangements. Suppliers are non-exclusive and could engage with competitors and prioritise supplies to their other customers. Suppliers have not terminated arrangements at short notice in the last three Fiscals.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on third-party suppliers with no firm commitments or exclusive arrangements

internal_operational.detail: The business is primarily focused on manufacturing and supplying automotive components to customers and OEMs engaged in the automobile sector and is heavily dependent on the performance of the Indian automotive sector, whose demand is cyclical and subject to government policy changes, regulatory or industry requirement changes and competing technologies including electric vehicles.
internal_operational.title: Revenue concentration in the automotive sector

internal_operational.detail: As a precision engineered component manufacturer the Company warrants conformity to customer specifications and drawings and continued usage of the product for a specified time or cycles. Product defects or failure to comply with quality or regulatory standards may lead to cancellation of existing and future orders, product recalls, warranty and liability claims, repair or replacement costs, regulatory consequences (warning letters, fines, injunctions, civil penalties, refusal or withdrawal of approvals, licence revocation, seizures or recalls, operating restrictions, criminal prosecutions) and third-party personal injury or property damage claims. Guarantees for quality and delivery obligations may or may not be capped. Products are bespoke and generally not standardised for open-market sale, so cancellation, delay or modification after production commences may cause inventory accumulation, write-offs or loss of revenue. Long useful life means latent defects may only become apparent after several years.
internal_operational.evidence: Risk factor 16: 'We have had warranty claims made against our products in the ordinary course of our business.' Guarantees for quality and delivery related obligations 'may or may not be capped'.
internal_operational.title: Strict customer performance requirements - quality, delivery, recalls, warranty and liability claims

internal_operational.detail: Third parties could pass off their own, counterfeit or pirated products as the Company's, reducing market share and harming goodwill. As on the date of the RHP the Company has applied for registration of one trademark whose status is 'Formalities Chk Pass'; if unregistered, rights are limited to common law rights, enforcement against third parties may be difficult, and rebranding costs may arise. Technical knowledge (engineering drawings, data, manufacturing processes, materials expertise, machine building and automation capabilities) may be leaked inadvertently or wilfully; a significant number of employees have access to confidential design and product information and may join competitors. Designs and products are not patented, so there may be no recourse against copies.
internal_operational.evidence: Risk factor 19: 'we have applied for the registration of one trademark for which the current status is Formalities Chk Pass'; 'our designs and products are not patented and thus, we may have no recourse against copies of our products and designs'.
internal_operational.title: Counterfeit products, leakage of technical know-how and unregistered intellectual property

internal_operational.detail: The workforce comprises both employees and contract workmen engaged through independent contractors. Availability of skilled and unskilled contract workmen at commercially reasonable rates is critical, and inability to obtain or retain them could affect production schedules. Manufacturing processes are increasingly reliant on technology-driven systems that contract workmen may be unable to operate effectively. Applicable labour laws may require the Company to pay wages of such labourers on contractor default, with recovery uncertain, and adverse regulatory or court orders on contract labour arrangements could increase operating costs and reduce workforce flexibility.
internal_operational.evidence: Risk factor 21: 'As at March 31, 2026, we engage over 800 contract workmen'. Contract labour charges for Fiscal 2024, Fiscal 2025, Fiscal 2026: Rs.1,293.79 lakhs, Rs.1721.51 lakhs, Rs.2538.43 lakhs. Employee benefit expenses: Rs.1657.87 lakhs, Rs.2011.88 lakhs, Rs.2599.94 lakhs.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on contract labour

internal_operational.detail: Manufacturing facility II (Gat No. 251/1, Plot No. 9, 10, 11, 13 (old GAT No. 2787/1), Talegaon Chakan Road, Kharabwadi, Chakan Industrial Area, Pune, Maharashtra, 410501) and proposed manufacturing facilities III and IV (Gat No. 382, 383, 386, 387, 312 Village, Tal. Khed, Dist. Pune 410501 and Gat No. 201/1, Village Mahalunge, Tal. Khed, Dist. Pune 410501) are held on lease for a period of 5 years, subject to renewal on mutual agreement with the licensor. Inability to renew, deficiency in the title of the leasehold property, challenge to the lessor's ownership or lapse of the lease may require vacating the premises and disrupt operations. No instances of leases not being renewed in the past three Financial Years.
internal_operational.evidence: Risk factor 23: leases 'for a period of 5 years'; 'we have not faced any such instances where our leases were not renewed in the past three Financial Years.'
internal_operational.title: Manufacturing facilities on leasehold premises

internal_operational.detail: Manufacturing facilities in Pune are subject to stringent labour legislation covering establishment of unions, dispute resolution, employee removal and retrenchment obligations. Labour unrest, work stoppages or slowdowns may disrupt operations, cause penalties for late delivery and damage reputation with customers. Wage settlement agreements (revised wage structures, ex-gratia payments, attendance bonuses, insurance enhancements) and collective bargaining renegotiations may increase labour costs and reduce flexibility to adjust headcount or salaries.
internal_operational.evidence: Risk factor 24: 'As of March 31, 2026, six of our employees were members of labour unions.'
internal_operational.title: Unionised employees and exposure to industrial unrest and wage costs

internal_operational.detail: The Company relies on third-party transportation and logistics providers engaged on a need-based basis, with no long-term or definitive agreements. The value of goods transported is typically significantly higher than the transportation charges payable, limiting recovery on damage, delay, loss or theft. Disruptions from increases in fuel costs, transportation strikes, accidents, adverse weather, lockouts or infrastructure constraints could delay contract execution, increase costs, damage or lose goods, and prolonged disruption could lead to contract termination, customer penalties or legal claims.
internal_operational.evidence: Risk factor 25: 'We do not maintain in-transit insurance for the transportation of such goods.'
internal_operational.title: Dependence on third parties for transportation and delivery; no in-transit insurance

internal_operational.detail: Insurance held includes Commercial Package Insurance Policy, Comprehensive General Liability Insurance Policy, Group Health Insurance Policy, Liberty Group Personal Accident Policy, Employee Insurance Compensation Policy and auto secure standalone own damage private car policy. No insurance has been obtained for the property at Gat No. 382, 383, 386, 387, 312 Village, Tal. Khed, Dist. Pune 410501 and Gat No. 201/1, Village Mahalunge, Tal. Khed, Dist. Pune 41050, which the Company plans to insure upon installation of machinery and commencement of production. No Key Man Insurance policy and no machinery breakdown insurance policy have been obtained.
internal_operational.evidence: Risk factor 27: 'the Company has not obtained any Key Man Insurance policy and machinery breakdown insurance policy.'
internal_operational.title: Insurance coverage may be inadequate; uninsured properties and no key man or machinery breakdown cover

internal_operational.detail: Manufacturing facilities require power and water and energy costs represent a significant portion of production costs. Rising energy or water costs may not be recoverable through product prices, and disruption of electricity or water supply may force reliance on alternative sources that may not consistently meet requirements, causing production shutdowns, restart costs and loss of production in progress.
internal_operational.evidence: Risk factor 28: 'For Fiscals 2024, 2025 and 2026, our power and fuel charges were Rs.1116.81 lakhs, Rs.1384.99 lakhs, and Rs.1969.97 lakhs, constituting 6.43%, 6.24%, and 6.70% respectively, of our total income.'
internal_operational.title: Power and water requirements; energy a significant portion of production cost

internal_operational.detail: Operations depend on IT systems susceptible to malfunctions and interruptions; design and engineering facilities comprise IT enabled processes and design software. Disruption may arise from human error, natural disasters, electrical or telecommunication outages, sabotage, computer viruses, hacking, cyber-attacks or loss of support services from third parties such as internet service providers, impairing the ability to plan, track, record and analyse work in progress and sales, process financial information, manage product lifecycle, creditors and debtors, payables and inventory.
internal_operational.title: Failure or disruption of information technology systems

internal_operational.detail: Major projects have been awarded in the states of Maharashtra, Karnataka, Punjab, Haryana and Gujarat, exposing operations to local and regional economic and weather conditions, natural disasters, demographic changes and other unforeseen events, and to social, political or economic disruption or state or local policy changes in this region. No such adverse situations were experienced in the last three fiscal years.
internal_operational.title: Geographic concentration of business in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Punjab, Haryana and Gujarat

internal_operational.detail: Manufacturing operations are subject to breakdowns or failures of plant and machinery, power supply interruptions, process failures, industrial or workplace accidents, labour unrest or disputes, natural disasters, epidemics or pandemics and regulatory directives, which could cause partial or complete shutdowns, production delays or operational inefficiencies. Certain customers may impose penalties, liquidated damages or other contractual consequences for stoppage or disruption caused by delayed delivery, quality issues or defects. Disruption could lower production volumes and capacity utilisation, raising per-unit costs. Except for the temporary suspension of operations during the nationwide COVID-19 lockdown between March 2020 and May 2020, no material shutdowns or disruptions have been experienced.
internal_operational.evidence: Risk factor 32: 'Except for the temporary suspension of operations during the nationwide lockdown imposed by the Government of India in response to the COVID-19 pandemic between March 2020 and May 2020, we have not experienced any material shutdowns or disruptions at our manufacturing facilities.'
internal_operational.title: Shutdown or disruption at manufacturing facilities

internal_operational.detail: The Company operates from two manufacturing facilities in India. Profitability depends on maintaining high levels of capacity utilisation, which is affected by product mix, accuracy of demand forecasting, uninterrupted operations, raw material availability and industry or market conditions. In case of oversupply in the industry or lack of demand, capacity additions may be under-utilised, adversely impacting revenue and profitability.
internal_operational.evidence: Risk factor 35 capacity utilisation, 2025-26 / 2024-25 / 2023-24: Melting - Installed Capacity (MT) 13800 | 9300 | 7800; Actual Production (MT) 10982 | 6704 | 6036; Utilization (%) 80% | 72% | 77%. Casting & Finishing - Installed Capacity (MT) 6000 | 4800 | 3900; Actual Production (MT) 5049 | 3352 | 3018; Utilization (%) 84% | 70% | 77%.
internal_operational.title: Under-utilisation of existing and expanded manufacturing capacities

internal_operational.detail: Success depends to a large extent on the continued services of Directors, Individual Promoters, Key Managerial Personnel, Senior Management and other personnel with technical expertise. The market for qualified professionals is competitive and retention may require increased compensation and benefits. The specialised skills required are difficult and time-consuming to acquire and in short supply, and a long period is required to hire and train replacement personnel. Loss of senior management could impair key customer relationships forged by them.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on Directors, Promoters, Key Managerial Personnel, Senior Management and technical personnel

internal_operational.detail: The Corporate Promoter and individual promoters Rahul Sohanlal Ranka, Vaishali Dakshendra Agrawal, Dakshendra Brijballabh Agrawal and Bhavya Dakshendra Agrawal are not the original promoters of the Company, though associated with it for more than 5 years. Promoters Dakshendra Brijballabh Agrawal and Bhavya Dakshendra Agrawal do not have prior experience in the Company's line of business and the corporate promoter does not have a track record in this industry. There is no assurance that future performance will be consistent with past financial performance.
internal_operational.evidence: Risk factor 45: 'they collectively hold 82.63% of the equity share capital of the Company'; experience - Anil Shivajirao Kulkarni around 32 years, Jayshree Anil Kulkarni 17 years, Sanket Anil Kulkarni 16 years, Rahul Sohanlal Ranka 25 years in die casting industry; Vaishali Dakshendra Agrawal 17 years in the field of finance.
internal_operational.title: Corporate Promoter and certain individual Promoters are not the original promoters and have limited experience in the line of business

internal_operational.detail: Information on installed capacity and capacity utilisation in the RHP is based on assumptions, estimates and methodologies adopted by management and considered by the chartered engineer. Actual production levels and capacity utilisation may differ materially from stated installed capacity or historical utilisation levels; capacity utilisation is not a standardised measure and may be calculated differently across industries, geographies and product categories, so comparisons with other companies may not be meaningful and undue reliance should not be placed on this data.
internal_operational.title: Installed capacity and capacity utilisation information based on assumptions and estimates

internal_operational.detail: Manufacturing operations increasingly rely on digital systems including computer aided design systems and information technology systems supporting design, production planning, quality control and inventory management. Exposures include unauthorized access or attempted breaches, network intrusions or denial-of-service attacks, malware, ransomware, and data loss, corruption or theft, which could disrupt manufacturing operations, impair quality control or production scheduling, delay order fulfilment, compromise sensitive business, technical or customer information, and cause non-compliance with customer specifications, contractual obligations, data protection requirements or applicable regulations.
internal_operational.title: Cyber security and data protection risk from reliance on digital and connected technologies

internal_operational.detail: Employee misconduct or errors could expose the Company to business risks or losses including regulatory sanctions and serious harm to reputation, and precautions may not be effective in all cases. Historically the Company has not experienced any material instances of employee misconduct or errors that subjected it to claims or proceedings for alleged negligence, regulatory action, litigation, claims for damages or customer indemnification obligations. Any claims or damages, if imposed, will be paid from internal accruals and no IPO proceeds (including the portion allocated toward General Corporate Purposes) will be utilized for this purpose.
internal_operational.evidence: Risk factor 56: 'Any claims or damages, if imposed, will be paid from the internal accruals of the company, and no IPO proceeds (including the portion allocated toward General Corporate Purposes) will be utilized for this purpose.'
internal_operational.title: Employee misconduct or errors

internal_operational.detail: Operations involve interactions with customers, suppliers, service providers, workers, employees and others, exposing the Company to unauthorized access, data sharing or alteration of sensitive information which may lead to data breaches or inadvertent disclosure of confidential information to competitors, regulatory authorities or third parties. Preventive and detection mechanisms, including internal controls, monitoring systems and disciplinary measures, may not be entirely effective or scale proportionately with business growth. No material instances of such events in the past three fiscal years.
internal_operational.evidence: Risk factor 57: 'Although we have not experienced any material instances of such events in the past three fiscal years'.
internal_operational.title: Fraudulent transactions and illegal activity affecting sensitive stakeholder information

internal_operational.detail: India's physical infrastructure is in a developing phase compared to that of many developed nations. Any congestion or disruption in port, rail and road networks, the electricity grid, communication systems or other public facilities could disrupt normal business activity, harm the national economy, disrupt transportation of goods and supplies and add costs to doing business in India.
internal_operational.title: Extent and reliability of Indian infrastructure

strategy_growth.detail: The Company intends to scale up annual production capacity by establishing a new manufacturing facility at Gat Nos. 382, 383, 386, 387 and 312, Village Khed, Taluka Khed, District Pune 410501, Maharashtra, utilizing the net proceeds from the IPO; the premises are held on lease under an agreement dated April 23, 2025 for five years commencing September 1, 2025 to August 30, 2030, with first right to the Company to continue thereafter, subject to renewal on mutual agreement. It also proposes to establish a magnesium casting facility at Gat No. 201/1, Village Mahalunge, Taluka Khed, District Pune 410501, marking entry into a new segment distinct from existing aluminium casting operations, with limited prior experience in magnesium casting and risks relating to technology stabilisation, process optimisation, quality control, raw material sourcing, skilled manpower availability and customer acceptance. Implementation risks include delays in obtaining governmental, statutory, environmental and customer/OEM approvals, delays in securing utilities such as electricity connections, force majeure events, site-related accidents or third-party claims and constraints in availability or timely deployment of funds, potentially increasing pre-operative expenses, project costs, interest and finance charges, working capital requirements and compliance costs. No material delays or cost overruns were experienced in the last three Fiscal years.
strategy_growth.evidence: Risk factor 6: lease 'agreement dated April 23, 2025 for a period of five years commencing from September 1, 2025 to August 30, 2030'; 'Although we have not experienced material delays or cost overruns in the last three Fiscal years'.
strategy_growth.title: Proposed expansion of manufacturing facilities in Pune subject to delays and cost overruns; entry into magnesium casting

strategy_growth.detail: Realisation of future sales from awarded business or new business is subject to the accuracy of customer estimates of volumes to be produced and sold and the timing of production. The Company participates in a lengthy and rigorous vendor selection process. Customers may delay or cancel the launch of a new vehicle or product for which the Company has been awarded a contract, or divert from domestic suppliers to global players pursuant to changes in geopolitical scenarios; without firm commitment long-term supply agreements there may be no recourse. Growth projections are based in part on customer volume projections provided under letters of intent or purchase orders that carry no commitment to purchase the quantities specified.
strategy_growth.title: Incremental business pipeline may not be indicative of future growth or realised revenue

strategy_growth.detail: Competition in India and overseas is based on product quality and reliability, breadth of product range, product design and innovation, technology, manufacturing capabilities, scope and quality of service, price and brand recognition. Some competitors have greater financial, technical and/or marketing resources enabling acquisitions, international growth funding, faster response to technological changes and more diversified geographies and product portfolios, and some may produce similar or equivalent products at lower cost. Price pressures are expected to increase as customers expand their manufacturing footprints, providing opportunities for local manufacturers. Manufacturers not currently competing could expand their product portfolios or establish relationships with the Company's customers that reduce or entirely replace its business.
strategy_growth.title: Competition in the highly competitive precision components industry

strategy_growth.detail: New products that customers commission the Company to develop and manufacture often involve significant initial investments and pre-production expenditures, including costs relating to product design and development, material sourcing, testing and validation in accordance with customer specifications and approval processes, and establishment of additional production lines or new manufacturing facilities. Inability to recover these initial investments, manage labour and equipment resources efficiently or accurately estimate time and resources, or discontinuation of new products, reduced OEM volumes or transition to alternate suppliers, may adversely affect results of operations particularly in the short term.
strategy_growth.title: Initial investment requirements and operational inefficiencies for new products and OEM approval processes

strategy_growth.detail: The Company proposes to acquire machinery and equipment for setting up its manufacturing facility. It has identified the required machinery and obtained quotations from suppliers, but final purchase orders have not yet been placed for all such machinery and equipment. It is subject to risks from inflation in machinery and equipment prices; since funding is from IPO proceeds, any delay in access to those proceeds would delay order placement, and supplier delivery delays may delay implementation of the expansion plan. Quotations relied upon are valid for a specific period and may lapse, leading to possible cost escalation, increase in project cost and cost overruns affecting profitability.
strategy_growth.evidence: Risk factor 31: machinery and equipment aggregating to Rs.11043.08 lakhs; 'we have placed orders aggregating to Rs.3161.16 lakhs, representing approximately 28.63% of the proposed capital expenditure against which an advance payment of Rs.2284.41 lakhs has been made.'
strategy_growth.title: No definitive arrangements for certain Objects; machinery orders largely not yet placed

strategy_growth.detail: Changes in consumer preferences, evolving regulatory and industry standards and advancements in competing technologies may reduce demand for, or render obsolete, certain existing products. Consumer preferences are shifting towards fuel-efficient and environmentally friendly vehicles, and heightened emission regulation with volatile fuel prices pressures the automotive industry to reduce carbon dioxide emissions. The Company may not adequately or timely respond to market developments including increasing penetration of battery electric vehicles and other alternative technologies in India and international markets, may be required to obtain licenses for third-party technologies not available on commercially reasonable terms, or to develop substitute technologies involving significant time, effort and expense.
strategy_growth.title: Failure to adapt to industry trends and evolving technologies

strategy_growth.detail: There is no assurance that past levels of revenue and profit margins or profit growth can be sustained. A number of strategic initiatives are in initial stages with no assurance of long-term success. Growth may not be sustainable due to execution capability, ability to bid and win new orders, ability to maintain customer satisfaction, ability to mobilize sufficient working capital, macroeconomic factors such as decline in global economic conditions, competition with players in organized and unorganized segments, the greater difficulty of growing at sustained rates from a larger revenue base, inability to control expenses and availability of resources for growth.
strategy_growth.evidence: Risk factor 49: 'our revenue from operations for Fiscal 2024, Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2026 was Rs. 17372.22 lakhs, Rs. 22199.93 lakhs and Rs. 29385.54 lakhs, respectively.'
strategy_growth.title: Inability to grow, sustain or manage revenue from operations, profitability or operations

strategy_growth.detail: As part of its long-term business strategy the Company may explore opportunities to expand its presence in existing geographies or enter new markets both within India and overseas. Expansion into new jurisdictions may expose it to complex management, legal, tax and economic risks arising from unfamiliar regulatory environments, collaboration with international partners and adaptation to different technical standards and customer expectations, including compliance with local laws and technical standards, complex tax and cost structures, regulatory barriers and trade restrictions, and cultural, language and operational differences.
strategy_growth.title: International market expansion risks

strategy_growth.detail: Industry information included in the RHP has been derived from publicly available industry reports and/or websites, which are subject to various limitations and based upon subjective assumptions. The Company has not independently verified data from such industry reports and other sources; accuracy, completeness and underlying assumptions are not guaranteed and dependability cannot be assured, and the statistics may be inaccurate or not comparable to statistics produced for other economies.
strategy_growth.title: Industry information derived from publicly available industry reports and websites

strategy_growth.detail: The Indian economy and capital markets are influenced by economic, political and market conditions in India and globally. Factors identified include epidemics, pandemics or other public health concerns; the macroeconomic climate including any increase in Indian interest rates or inflation; exchange rate fluctuations, imposition of currency controls and restrictions on the right to convert or repatriate currency or export/import assets; scarcity of credit or other financing in India; prevailing income conditions among Indian consumers and corporates; volatility in trading activity on India's principal stock exchanges; changes in India's tax, trade, fiscal or monetary policies; political instability, terrorism or military conflict in India or the region; occurrence of natural or man-made disasters such as typhoons, flooding, earthquakes and fires; civil unrest, acts of violence, terrorist attacks, regional conflicts or war; prevailing regional or global economic conditions including in India's principal export markets and imposition of tariffs or other trade measures by trading partners such as the United States; downgrading of India's debt rating; international business practices conflicting with other customs or legal requirements including anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws; logistical and communications challenges; financial instability in financial markets; difficulty in developing partnerships with local businesses; being subject to the jurisdiction of foreign courts; and other significant regulatory or economic developments in or affecting India or its manufacturing sector.
strategy_growth.title: Political, economic or other factors beyond the Company's control affecting India

concerns_observed: ₹7,881.92 lakhs of the ₹11,043.08 lakh estimated project cost — 49 separate line items including VMC machines ₹2,003.05 lakhs, LPDC machines ₹861.40 lakhs, HMC machines ₹920.40 lakhs, ZEISS CMMs ₹344.39 lakhs and tilt-GDC machines ₹469.64 lakhs — rests on vendor QUOTATIONS ONLY, dated April to July 2026 and generally valid 5 to 6 months (one 90 days, one 7 months), several therefore expiring around the deployment window. The DRHP states no definitive agreements have been entered into with the vendors, that actual cost and actual supplier may vary, and that management retains flexibility to change machinery, vendor or quantity; its own risk factor puts orders placed at ₹3,161.16 lakhs, approximately 28.63% of the proposed capital expenditure.

Trade receivables outstanding beyond one year stepped up sharply in FY26: the 1-2 year bucket of undisputed receivables considered good went ₹48.25 lakhs (FY24) → ₹12.27 lakhs (FY25) → ₹357.74 lakhs (FY26), alongside 2-3 year ₹12.73 / ₹12.74 / ₹8.52 lakhs and over-3-year ₹0.38 / ₹3.13 / ₹3.13 lakhs, and a ₹47.66 lakh doubtful-receivable deduction appears in the FY26 schedule bringing the 1-2 year line to ₹310.08 lakhs net. Debtor days moved 42 → 58 → 64 and total receivables 11.45% → 15.98% → 17.63% of revenue (₹1,989.15 → ₹3,548.11 → ₹5,181.59 lakhs).

Litigation sits almost entirely off the balance sheet and on the promoters: ₹1,880.39 lakhs is the aggregate amount involved in proceedings AGAINST the Promoters (1 criminal, 12 tax, 2 material civil), against ₹7.13 lakhs against the Company (2 tax, 1 material civil), ₹197.61 lakhs against a Group Company (1 tax), ₹15.67 lakhs against Directors other than Promoters (2 tax) and ₹95.46 lakhs in 2 criminal proceedings filed BY those Directors. The Board's own materiality thresholds set on December 17, 2025 were 2% of turnover ₹587.71 lakhs, 2% of net worth ₹266.32 lakhs and 5% of average absolute PAT ₹118.22 lakhs — the promoter block is a multiple of all three.

Both borrowing legs rose steeply into the raise and the restated balance sheet prints no combined borrowings line: Long-term Borrowings ₹816.81 → ₹1,195.46 → ₹1,946.63 lakhs and Short-term Borrowings ₹611.24 → ₹758.08 → ₹2,169.24 lakhs across FY24-FY26, with short-term borrowings more than tripling in the pre-IPO year. Total financial indebtedness is separately stated at ₹7,082.56 lakhs as of June 30, 2026 — three months after the FY26 balance-sheet date — including a cash credit drawn to ₹1,376.39 lakhs of ₹1,500.00 lakhs sanctioned and an overdraft at ₹82.53 lakhs of ₹100.00 lakhs, both repayable on demand, and personal guarantees from Promoters Anil Shivajirao Kulkarni, Rahul Sohanlal Ranka, Sanket Anil Kulkarni and Jayshree Anil Kulkarni.

Auditor-certified promoter average cost of acquisition is ₹4.87 (Jayshree Anil Kulkarni), ₹5.01 (Anil Shivajirao Kulkarni), ₹5.21 (Sanket Anil Kulkarni), ₹5.76 (Rahul Sohanlal Ranka) and ₹7.13 (Bhavya Financial Services), against the highest price the document itself records — the July 13-14, 2026 promoter transfers at ₹271 and ₹301; the Company carries an explicit risk factor that the promoters' average cost may be lower than the ₹10 face value. Trade receivables beyond one year jumped in the year immediately preceding the Issue — the 1-2 year bucket from ₹12.27 lakhs to ₹357.74 lakhs — with a ₹47.66 lakh doubtful deduction appearing for the first time in the FY26 ageing schedule, while debtor days rose 42 → 58 → 64 and receivables reached 17.63% of revenue.

A sustained ROC and statutory-dues compliance pattern being regularised at the IPO: 14 delayed filings from 2 to 575 days (MGT-14 due 10/09/2024 filed 08/04/2026), Section 123(4) dividend-deposit failure in four consecutive Fiscals with adjudication filed, Section 203 CS non-appointment with compounding filed, unfiled CHG-1 charges, no audit trail in the accounting software for FY2024-25, and delayed PF, ESI, professional tax, GST and TDS filings in each of the last three years.

The entire 41,00,000-share Promoters' Contribution locked in for three years was allotted on November 25, 2025 at a price of ₹0 as a 3:5 bonus, five weeks after a private placement at ₹3,156 per ₹100-face-value share and a 100:10 sub-division — with auditor-certified promoter average acquisition costs of ₹4.87 to ₹7.13 and an explicit risk factor that this may be below the ₹10 face value.

Three promoter shareholders transferred shares on July 13-14, 2026 — Bhavya Financial Services 4,39,800 and Jayshree Anil Kulkarni 2,75,000 at ₹271, Rahul Sohanlal Ranka 1,99,800 plus 200 at ₹301 — within days of the July 22, 2026 RHP and within the six months preceding it, against those ₹4.87-₹7.13 average costs.

Untraceable statutory records spanning three decades: Form 5 for the March 31, 2000 authorised-capital increase, Form 2 for the November 22, 2002 allotment, Form 18 for the November 20, 2002 registered-office change and Form 32 for the September 01, 1993 Managing Director appointment, plus pre-2006 Form 8 charge filings, 2006-2011 Form 23B auditor appointments, FY1996-97 financial statements and the FY1999-2000 annual return; parts of the capital-history table rest on internal records, with a PCS search report dated March 13, 2026 unable to trace them.

Promoter-group entities supply a material share of inputs (FY26 goods purchases of ₹1,848.46, ₹638.31 and ₹566.44 lakhs plus ₹480.55 lakhs of labour charges, against ₹13,727.73 lakhs of raw material consumed) while none of the three group companies' reserves, sales, PAT, EPS or NAV appear in the RHP — they are posted on the issuer's website, which the RHP states does not form part of it.

Prior disqualification and struck-off history across the promoter group and board: Promoter/Non-Executive Director Vaishali Dakshendra Agrawal and SMP Shekhar Sharadchandra Dravid both on the disqualified-directors list from November 01, 2016 to October 31, 2021; Promoters Anil Shivajirao Kulkarni and Rahul Sohanlal Ranka formerly directors of struck-off Jayshree Die Castings; Independent Director Viren Ajit Joshi of two struck-off Vivaa entities.

The restated FY24-FY26 financial statements on which the Issue rests were prepared by a peer-reviewed Chartered Accountants firm that is not the statutory auditor, attributed to the statutory auditor's preoccupation.
strengths_observed: Three straight years of revenue and profit expansion: revenue from operations ₹17,372.22 → ₹22,199.93 → ₹29,385.54 lakhs, EBITDA ₹2,745.29 → ₹3,988.50 → ₹5,177.65 lakhs, PAT ₹1,609.65 → ₹2,393.08 → ₹3,090.28 lakhs and restated EPS ₹11.76 → ₹17.48 → ₹21.90 across FY24-FY26, with the DRHP stating the Company remained profitable in each of the last three Fiscals.

RoNW of 23.21% (FY26), 27.76% (FY25) and 24.83% (FY24) against the DRHP's own peer table for the same year ended March 31, 2026 — Alicon Castalloy 5.48%, RICO Auto 6.68% and Endurance Technologies 13.91% — on a book value of ₹94.36 and EPS of ₹21.90 basic and diluted.

Capacity roughly doubled in two years while utilisation still improved: melting installed capacity 7,800 → 9,300 → 13,800 MT with actual production 6,036 → 6,704 → 10,982 MT (utilisation 77% / 72% / 80%), and casting & finishing 3,900 → 4,800 → 6,000 MT with production 3,018 → 3,352 → 5,049 MT (77% / 70% / 84%) — FY26 is the highest utilisation of the three years on the largest base. Unit I melting alone ran 4,200 → 4,800 → 6,000 MT at 81% / 81% / 91%.

Concentration fell on every disclosed axis over FY24-FY26: top-1 customer 41.94% → 34.63% → 31.75% of sales, top-5 84.42% → 78.41% → 74.72%, top-10 96.00% → 90.63% → 88.64% (₹26,048.14 lakhs in FY26); top-1 supplier 25.31% → 19.30% → 14.76% and top-10 65.66% → 59.28% → 57.17%; customer count rose from 39 in Fiscal 2024 to 58 in Fiscal 2026 with repeat business from 25 customers.

Mix diversifying away from the core automobile line: EV sector revenue share 6.13% → 8.75% → 9.81% (3-wheeler EV alone 5.64% → 9.19%) and non-automobile 14.00% → 19.21% → 17.61% (energy 9.82% → 10.53%, agriculture 1.08% → 2.75%, structural parts 1.10% → 1.98%), with the Company stating it recently entered the aerospace segment and obtained vendor approval from a customer.

The Issue is entirely a fresh issue of up to 53,10,000 Equity Shares with no offer for sale, taking pre-issue capital of 1,46,34,960 shares to up to 1,99,44,960 and promoter holding from 82.63% to 60.63%; the shareholding pattern shows '-' (nil) shares pledged or otherwise encumbered for Promoters & Promoter Group, Public and Total, 41,00,000 shares (20.56% of post-Issue capital) are locked in for 3 years as Promoters' Contribution, and CARE Ratings Limited is appointed Monitoring Agency.

Operating cash flow was positive in all three years — ₹1,626.81 / ₹1,587.37 / ₹2,379.80 lakhs — against PPE additions of ₹1,244.36 / ₹1,997.53 / ₹2,525.18 lakhs, and ₹2,284.41 lakhs of the Unit III project was already deployed per the statutory auditor's certificate dated July 14, 2026, with placed-order items 1 to 7 already delivered.

The entire ₹7,082.56 lakhs of financial indebtedness outstanding as of June 30, 2026 is from institutional lenders — State Bank of India, SIDBI, HSBC and HDFC Bank — at stated rates of 7.98% to 9.50%, with every facility recorded against a business purpose (vehicle, machinery, equipment, business, working capital, solar, ECLGS) and none flagged non-business.

Integrated melt-to-finished-component capability across GDC, LPDC and HPDC casting plus heat treatment, induction hardening, machining, assembly and testing over 600+ SKUs including safety-critical parts, supported by a 17-member design team using casting simulation, X-ray, CMM and 3D scanning, 54 of 216 full-time employees in quality assurance, and IATF 16949:2016 at both facilities alongside ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018.
